drafts.title: Is training a local AI on the 2018 International Building Code practical for floor plan analysis?
drafts.body:
I came across a post from mid-2025 where the author wanted to create a focused AI model trained specifically on the 2018 International Building Code (IBC) to analyze floor plans and provide building code feedback. The idea is to input a floor plan and get a code-based analysis directly from the model.

Given the specificity of the 2018 IBC text, is it practical to train a local LLM just on this document for such a task? Or would it be more efficient to rely on a cloud-based model like ChatGPT with carefully crafted prompts to interpret the code relative to floor plans? The source doesn't provide details on feasibility or performance, so I’m curious if anyone has insight into the tradeoffs between a local specialized model versus prompt engineering on a general model for this use case.

The question is whether it makes sense to train a local LLM on such a narrowly defined corpus, or if using a cloud model like ChatGPT with well-designed prompts could be just as effective or better.
